record.paper_title: Holomorphic mappings: Survey of some results and discussion of open problems
record.original_question: Let D be a normal-crossings divisor in P^n, and let f: C -> P^n \ D be a holomorphic curve whose image misses D. If deg(D) is at least n+2, must the image f(C) lie in an algebraic subvariety of P^n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{P}^n$ denote complex projective space of dimension $n\geq 2$, and let $D\subset \mathbb{P}^n$ be a normal-crossings divisor (i.e.\ at each point of its support, $D$ is locally cut out by a product of distinct smooth analytic branches meeting transversally). Write $\deg(D)$ for the degree of $D$ as a hypersurface in $\mathbb{P}^n$. Suppose $f:\mathbb{C}\to \mathbb{P}^n\setminus D$ is a nonconstant holomorphic map whose image avoids $D$.

Question: If $\deg(D)\geq n+2$, must the image $f(\mathbb{C})$ be contained in a proper algebraic subvariety of $\mathbb{P}^n$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a form of the logarithmic Green–Griffiths / Lang conjecture for complements of normal-crossings divisors in projective space. Known unconditional algebraic-degeneracy results require very high degree bounds (e.g. effective bounds of the form $d \geq n^{(n+1)^{n+5}}$ for generic hypersurfaces), and the sharp threshold $\deg(D)\geq n+2$ remains unresolved in general; only partial results (generic divisors, special configurations of hyperplanes/hypersurfaces) are available.

status_evidence.title: Effective algebraic degeneracy (Diverio–Merker–Rousseau)
status_evidence.snippet: Nonconstant entire holomorphic curves in a generic projective hypersurface of degree d ≥ n^{(n+1)^{n+5}} are algebraically degenerate.
status_evidence.claim: Algebraic degeneracy is known only for very large degree bounds, not for the sharp value n+2.

status_evidence.title: Entire holomorphic curves into projective spaces intersecting a generic hypersurface of high degree
status_evidence.snippet: Algebraic degeneracy for entire curves omitting a generic hypersurface holds for sufficiently high degree.
status_evidence.claim: Results are conditional on genericity and high degree, leaving the n+2 threshold open.
